Samsung launches One UI 9.5 beta program, confirms eligible markets and key features

By
Anvinraj Valiyathara
-
Nov 18, 2026
Advertisement
Facebook
Twitter
ReddIt
Copy URL
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:04
    Instaread

    Samsung has been steadily preparing its next software update following early One UI 9.5 beta preparations, feature rumors, and a recently surfaced eligible devices list. After wrapping up much of its One UI 9 rollout, the company has now officially kicked off the One UI 9.5 beta program ahead of its stable debut.

    One UI 9.5 beta features and improvements

    The One UI 9.5 beta brings meaningful upgrades across camera controls, health tracking, accessibility, and privacy. In the camera app, key settings and a zoom bar now sit on a single screen for faster adjustments, while enhanced Pro and Pro Video modes add customizable controls and presets on supported devices (excluding Pro Lite and Pro Video Lite models).

    Also Read
    Samsung One UI 9.0: Release date, supported devices, and new features

    Samsung Health gains Mindful Note for guided or freeform journaling – though it is not supported on Galaxy Watch – alongside an expanded Medications feature for tracking prescriptions, supplements, and reminders across more markets. Accessibility also improves with a floating shortcut for frequent controls and notification-panel adjustments for hearing aid volume and sound routing. Perhaps the biggest everyday addition for privacy-conscious buyers is native App Lock, which secures individual apps via biometrics or screen lock while hiding their notification content and widgets without relying on Secure Folder.

    One UI 9.5 beta availability and how to join

    The One UI 9.5 beta program is live starting today for Galaxy S26, Galaxy S26+, and Galaxy S26 Ultra owners in Germany, India, South Korea, Poland, the UK, and the US. Eligible users can enroll directly through the Samsung Members app, then download the test build via Settings > Software update. For users who prefer to wait for a stable release, One UI 9.5 is expected to debut officially alongside Samsung’s next flagship generation early next year, giving Galaxy S26 owners an early preview of the refinements first.
